verdict.rationale: Gmail has a documented REST API covering core mailbox operations: messages, threads, labels, drafts, sending, filters, delegates, signatures and push notifications. Nothing in the evidence shows UI parity. UI features such as snooze, Undo Send, offline Outbox and Gemini summarize/draft/organize have no documented API equivalent. A hands-on developer noted that thread listing omits message details, which makes building a full client hard. Missing for 10: API equivalents for snooze, undo send and Gemini AI actions; an explicit parity statement or machine-readable API spec; complete thread data in list calls.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The Gmail API lets you view and manage Gmail mailbox data like threads, messages, and labels.
Delegates can read, send, and delete messages, as well as view and add contacts on behalf of the delegator's account.
Advanced rules configured for an account that evaluate incoming messages against specific matching criteria (like sender, subject, or size).
Creates a draft with the `DRAFT` label.
The Gmail API provides server push notifications that let you watch for changes to Gmail mailboxes.
Building a full client is hard because listing threads doesn't return the messages, so participants and timestamps aren't available.
